examples.ko: 아이가 누운 지 오 분 만에 꿈나라였어요.
examples.en: The child was in dreamland within five minutes of lying down.

examples.ko: 동생은 지금 꿈나라에서 놀고 있나 봐요.
examples.en: My younger sibling must be off in dreamland now.
I brush my teeth before going off to dreamland.

examples.ko: 그림책 속 꿈나라 이야기를 읽어 줬어요.
examples.en: I read a story about dreamland from a picture book.
I should head to dreamland early today.

examples.ko: 꿈나라로 가는 기차가 나오는 동화를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like fairy tales with a train to dreamland.

explain: 잠자는 동안 가는 상상의 세계를 말해서, 아이들 이야기나 잠자리 인사에 자주 나와요. 어른도 '벌써 꿈나라예요'처럼 장난스럽게 쓰기도 해요. 진지한 글보다 부드럽고 귀여운 말투에 어울려요.

phrases.example: 피곤했는지 저녁도 안 먹고 꿈나라로 갔어요.
phrases.en: He must have been tired, because he went off to sleep without eating dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잠들다'를 귀엽고 부드럽게 돌려 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cute, soft way of saying someone falls asleep.

explain_en: It is an imaginary world you go to while asleep, so it often appears in children's stories and bedtime talk. Adults also use it playfully, as in '벌써 꿈나라예요'. It suits a soft, cute tone more than serious writing.

examples.en: That singer debuted at seventeen.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 새 아이돌 그룹이 데뷔해요.
examples.en: A new idol group debuts next month.
I also want to debut as an actor someday.

examples.ko: 그 가수가 데뷔한 지 벌써 십 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It's already been ten years since that singer debuted.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 올해 영화로 데뷔할 예정이에요.
examples.en: That director is set to make a film debut this year.
Before debuting, they spent a long time as a trainee.

explain: 가수, 배우, 작가, 선수가 처음 무대나 경기에 나설 때 써요. 회사에 처음 들어가는 건 '입사하다'를 써서 구분해요. '데뷔 10년 차'처럼 활동한 해를 세는 말로도 써요.

phrases.en: Today is that singer's debut stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 사람들 앞에 서는 무대를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the first stage performance in front of an audience.

phrases.en: That actor is in the tenth year since debuting this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 데뷔한 뒤 활동한 해를 셀 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to count the years of activity since debuting.

phrases.en: That singer will debut next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 데뷔할 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for talking about a planned future debut.

explain_en: It is for singers, actors, writers, and athletes appearing publicly for the first time. Starting at a company is '입사하다', not '데뷔하다'. It also counts career years, as in '데뷔 10년 차' (in the tenth year since debut).

examples.en: On the weekend I went to a car wash and cleaned my car.
This car wash is self-service, so it's cheap.

examples.ko: 세차장 앞에 차가 줄을 서 있어요.
examples.en: Cars are lined up in front of the car wash.

examples.ko: 비 오기 전에 세차장에서 세차하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't wash your car at the car wash right before it rains.

examples.ko: 집 근처에 새로 생긴 세차장이 깨끗해요.
examples.en: The newly opened car wash near my house is clean.
I opened a map app to find a car wash.

explain: 차를 씻는 곳이에요. 직접 씻는 곳은 '셀프 세차장', 기계가 자동으로 씻는 곳은 '자동 세차'라고도 말해요. 차를 씻는 일은 '세차하다', 손으로 직접 씻는 건 '손세차'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 집 근처에 셀프 세차장이 새로 생겼어요.
phrases.en: A new self-service car wash opened near my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손님이 직접 차를 씻는 곳이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A place where customers wash their cars themselves.

phrases.example: 비가 온 뒤에 자동 세차를 했어요.
phrases.en: After the rain, I got an automatic car wash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 차를 씻어 주는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A way of washing in which a machine washes the car.

phrases.example: 세차장 이용 시간은 밤 열 시까지예요.
phrases.en: The car wash is open until 10 p.m.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문 여는 시간을 물을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when asking about opening hours.

explain_en: It is a place for washing cars. A place where you wash it yourself is a '셀프 세차장', and one with machines may be called '자동 세차'. Washing a car is '세차하다', and washing by hand is '손세차'.

examples.en: My younger sibling drew a cat in the sketchbook.
I went to the stationery store to buy a new sketchbook.

examples.ko: 스케치북이 거의 다 차서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: The sketchbook is almost full, so I need to buy a new one.

examples.ko: 이 스케치북은 종이가 두꺼워서 물감을 써도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: This sketchbook has thick paper, so it is fine to use paint.

examples.ko: 아이가 스케치북 한 권을 한 달 만에 다 썼어요.
examples.en: The child used up a whole sketchbook in a month.
I took a sketchbook and colored pencils out of my bag.

explain: 스케치북은 그림을 그리는 공책이에요. 글씨를 쓰거나 문제를 푸는 공책은 '연습장'이나 '공책'이라고 해요. 세는 단위는 '권'이어서 '스케치북 한 권'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 스케치북 한 권을 다 쓰고 새로 샀어요.
phrases.en: I used up one sketchbook and bought a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스케치북은 '권'으로 세요. 숫자를 먼저 말하지 않고 '한 권'을 뒤에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sketchbooks are counted with '권'. The number goes after the noun.

phrases.en: I drew a flower in my sketchbook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림을 그리는 곳은 '-에'로 말해요. 그림은 '그리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place you draw is marked with '-에', and the verb is '그리다'.

phrases.en: I drew my first picture in the new sketchbook.
phrases.nuance_ko: '새'는 명사 앞에서 새것이라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '새' before a noun adds the meaning of 'new'.

explain_en: A 스케치북 is for drawing. A notebook for writing or working out problems is called '연습장' or '공책'. You count them with '권', as in '스케치북 한 권'.

examples.en: I made a cheese omelette for breakfast.
You make an omelette by beating eggs.
This restaurant's omelette is soft and delicious.
I put plenty of vegetables in the omelette.
I ordered an omelette and toast together.
I learned how to make an omelette from a video.

explain: 한국의 '계란말이'와 비슷하지만 다른 음식이에요. 계란말이는 돌돌 말아서 반찬으로 먹고, 오믈렛은 속을 채워 접어서 서양식으로 먹어요. 달걀은 '계란'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I ordered a vegetable omelette.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속에 들어가는 재료를 앞에 붙여 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the filling before the word to name the type.

phrases.en: I cooked an omelette in a frying pan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불에 익혀 만든다고 할 때 '굽다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 굽다 for cooking it over heat.

phrases.en: We shared a plate of omelette.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 셀 때 '접시'를 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 접시 to count a plate of food.

explain_en: It is similar to the Korean '계란말이' but a different dish. '계란말이' is rolled up and eaten as a side dish, while an omelette is folded around a filling and eaten Western-style. An egg is also called '계란'.

examples.en: The chairperson starts the meeting.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 위원장은 삼 학년 학생이에요.
examples.en: The head of our school committee is a third-year student.
We elected a new chairperson yesterday.
I will tell the chairperson first.
That person works as the head of the election committee.
Applause came after the chairperson finished speaking.

explain: 위원회의 가장 높은 사람의 직함이라서 '위원장님'처럼 '님'을 붙여 불러요. 회사는 '사장', 학교는 '교장'처럼 조직마다 책임자 이름이 달라요. 그 아래 자리는 '부위원장'이에요.

phrases.en: Chairperson, I'll give you today's meeting materials.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부르거나 높여서 말할 때 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '님' when addressing the person directly or speaking respectfully about them.

phrases.en: Minsu was chosen as the new chairperson.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투표나 회의로 위원장이 정해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a chairperson is chosen by a vote or meeting.

phrases.en: When the chairperson is absent, the vice chairperson runs the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위원장 바로 아래 자리라서 위원장을 도와요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the position right below the chairperson, who assists them.

explain_en: It is the title of the top person in a committee, so people add the honorific suffix when addressing the person. The head of a company or school has a different title, such as the words for president or principal. The position below is the vice chair.

dis.h: head of a committee or commission

p.n: 위원장 chairs a committee; 회장 is the head of a club or company.

examples.en: The autumn leaves turned orange.
I like clothes that have orange in them.

examples.ko: 해가 질 때 하늘이 주황과 분홍으로 물들어요.
examples.en: At sunset the sky is dyed orange and pink.
Orange comes out when you mix red and yellow.
Please paint it a color close to orange.

examples.ko: 주황도 노랑도 밝아서 눈에 잘 띄어요.
examples.en: Both orange and yellow are bright, so they stand out.

explain: '주황색'이라고도 하고 '오렌지색'이라고도 해요. 한자로 '주'는 빨강, '황'은 노랑이어서 빨강과 노랑 사이 색이에요. 과일 오렌지의 색뿐 아니라 감과 귤 색에도 써요.

phrases.en: I bought an orange bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주황'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요. 뒤에 명사가 올 때 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than 주황, and easy to use before a noun.

phrases.en: The orange umbrella is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주황색'과 뜻이 같고 조금 더 가벼운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 주황색, with a lighter feel.

phrases.en: I painted the wall orange.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 칠한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you paint something a color.

explain_en: You can say '주황색' or '오렌지색' as well. In the Chinese characters '주' is red and '황' is yellow, so it is the color between red and yellow. It is used not only for the fruit orange but for the color of persimmons and tangerines too.

dis.h: orange color; short form, used in compounds

p.n: 주황색 is the full form; 주황 sounds shorter and is often paired with 노랑.

examples.en: My grandfather passed away last year.

examples.ko: 아이는 하늘나라에 있는 엄마에게 편지를 썼어요.
examples.en: The child wrote a letter to her mother in heaven.
In the fairy tale, an angel who lives in heaven appears.
Grandfather, I hope you are happy in heaven too.

examples.ko: 저 구름 위에 하늘나라가 있을 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think there's a heavenly land above those clouds.
I watched a cartoon about the world in the sky.

explain: 종교에서 말하는 천국이나 동화 속 하늘 위의 세계를 부드럽게 말할 때 써요. 특히 돌아가신 분을 이야기할 때 '하늘나라에 계시다'처럼 쓰면 더 따뜻하게 들려요.

phrases.en: My grandmother passed away last winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '죽다' 대신 쓰는 부드럽고 조심스러운 표현이에요. 가족이나 가까운 사람의 죽음을 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft, gentle way to say someone died, used instead of '죽다'. Often used for family or close people.

explain_en: It softly refers to heaven in religion or a world in the sky in fairy tales. When speaking of someone who has passed away, saying '하늘나라에 계시다' sounds gentler and warmer.

examples.en: I hope to work in the marketing field.
It's a university many students hope to get into.

examples.ko: 여행을 희망하시면 이 종이에 이름을 써 주세요.
examples.en: If you'd like to go on the trip, please write your name on this paper.
My parents hope that I become a doctor.
I asked for Thursday as the interview date.
I don't wish to work overseas.

explain: 신청서나 면접에서는 '희망해요'를 쓰지만, 친구에게는 '원해요', '-고 싶어요'라고 해요. 명사 '희망'은 '희망이 있다/없다'처럼 앞으로 좋아질 거라는 믿음을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I really want this job.
phrases.nuance_ko: '희망하다'보다 일상적이어서 친구와 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than '희망하다', fine for talking with friends.

phrases.en: The job I hope for is teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태로 쓰면 신청서나 면접에서 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In this modifying form it sounds natural on forms and in interviews.

phrases.en: I don't wish to work night shifts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하지 않는다는 뜻을 공손하고 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite, formal way to say you do not want something.

explain_en: On forms and in interviews people use '희망해요', but with friends they say '원해요' or '-고 싶어요'. The noun '희망' also means hope that things will get better, as in '희망이 있다/없다'.

dis.h: formal: state a wish or request

p.n: 희망하다 sounds like a formal request; 바라다 is a softer, general wish.
